questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: How does stopping distance for motorcycles compare to stopping distance for cars?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Both take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance under normal conditions. However, wet pavement makes it harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes happen with riders who have less than six months of experience on the motorcycle they were riding.

questions.question: If your rear tire locks on good road surface, you should:

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on good road surface, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip from car drippings. This strip:

options.text: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided since other parts of the lane are cleaner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oily drippings from cars collect in the center of traffic lanes. On dry roads, this area still has enough grip for safe motorcycle riding. The oily strip is usually only two feet wide, so riders can position themselves to one side and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When a group of motorcyclists enters a highway or takes a curve, they should:

options.text: Ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride single-file.
questions.explanation: Although staggered formation is usually best, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: A rider uses a left arm bent at the elbow and pointing upward to signal a right turn or right lane change.

questions.question: If your front wheel starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Keep the front brake pressed and ride out the skid.
Keep the front brake pressed and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away and press it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and press it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake completely right away before pressing it again smoothly.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look where you want to go in turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look where you want to go in turns.
questions.explanation: Look through turns toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What is the proper footwear for riding a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes with short heels.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on rough surfaces. Tuck in laces so they don't get caught on anything.

questions.question: What should you do when taking a long motorcycle trip?

options.text: Skip rest breaks to save time.
Use caffeine if you feel sleepy.
Dress warmly to protect against cold wind and rain.
Ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect against cold wind and rain.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours a day and take rest breaks every two hours. Avoid caffeine and stimulants because fatigue gets worse when they wear off.

questions.question: Is wearing a riding jacket in hot weather a good idea?

options.text: Yes, it helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
No, it can cause heat-related problems.
Only if the jacket is light colored.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Always wear a riding jacket and long pants, even in hot weather. They protect you from injury in a crash and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: How long can the effects of marijuana last?
questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours.
questions.explanation: When smoked, marijuana starts affecting you within minutes and lasts two to four hours. When eaten, it takes over an hour to start working but can last more than six hours.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle in the lane when another vehicle is passing you?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding toward the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding away from them might tempt the driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite of the direction you want to turn.
Don't hold the grip because it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: At speeds faster than walking, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pressing the grip in the direction you want to turn makes the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: Helmeted riders are how many times more likely to survive a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a crash than not wearing one, at any speed.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. These signs tell you the traffic rules. You must follow the rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of proper riding clothes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Discomfort.
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you in a crash and protect you from bad weather like cold and wind. They provide comfort, not discomfort.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group ride?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way, they don't have to rush to keep up with the group. More experienced riders behind them can also watch and help them.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader, near the front of the group. This way, experienced riders at the back can watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider discourage other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Make angry gestures at other drivers.
Ride in a zigzag pattern across the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to prevent other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane
There is no single best position for all situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position for all situations.
questions.explanation: The best lane position changes depending on road and traffic conditions. Choose a position that keeps you safe, visible to others, and gives you room to escape if needed.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of rounded, or convex, motorcycle mirrors?

options.text: They are easy to adjust to immediately.
They make cars appear closer than they are.
They show a narrow view of the road behind you.
They make cars appear farther away than they are.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make cars appear farther away than they are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view than flat mirrors, but objects look farther away than they really are. You need to practice judging distances with these mirrors.

questions.question: Which of the following should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Block your access to an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your access to an escape route.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid blind spots, surface hazards, and wind blasts. Your lane position should discourage lane sharing and give you a way to escape if danger appears.
